memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Libnah, Ether, Ashan, Iphtah, Ashnah, Nezib, Keilah, Akzib and Mareshah—nine towns and their villages; Ekron, with its surrounding settlements and villages; west of Ekron, all that were in the vicinity of Ashdod, together with their villages; Ashdod, its surrounding settlements and villages; and Gaza, its settlements and villages, as far as the Wadi of Egypt and the coastline of the Mediterranean Sea - Josh 15:42-47 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The account rolls on through still more towns and regions, reaching all the way to the great sea. The sheer length of the list is itself a kind of sermon. God's generosity to Judah was not thin or grudging; it was abundant, spilling across region after region, more than could be quickly summarized.

We can lose sight of how much God gives when we are focused on what we lack. But a list like this, patiently naming gift after gift, invites us to consider the breadth of God's provision. He is not stingy toward His people. He gives fully, richly, more than we often stop to count. If Judah had paused to tally every town, they would have been overwhelmed by the scale of the inheritance God had granted.

The same is true for us, though we rarely notice. Every good and perfect gift comes down from the Father (Jas 1:17), and the sheer number of them would astonish us if we listed them out. Above all, in Christ, God has given us every spiritual blessing (Eph 1:3) — forgiveness, adoption, His Spirit, an eternal inheritance. When your eyes are fixed on what is missing, a list like Judah's towns gently turns you back to count instead the abundance God has already poured out.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you tend to focus more on what you lack or on what God has given?
- What might happen if you paused to count God's gifts one by one?
- How does the abundance of God's provision reshape your outlook today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me for dwelling on what I lack when You have given so abundantly. Open my eyes to count Your countless gifts, and above all the blessings I have in Christ. Amen.
